headline: Meta lets you opt out of AI training on smart glasses data
summary: Users can now prevent Meta from using visual data from AI experiences on smart glasses for product improvement, though some features may be affected.
details: Meta has begun rolling out a new setting for its smart glasses that allows users to opt out of having their visual data used for AI training. This option is accessible through the Meta AI app and requires the glasses to be connected to a phone.

The company is notifying glasses owners via pop-ups, explaining that opting out means visual data won't be stored after processing. While this preserves privacy, Meta warns that certain features, such as 'visual reminders,' might become unavailable.

The new setting is located within the glasses' settings under 'Meta AI,' where users can find the 'store visual data from AI experiences' option. This step must be repeated for each pair of glasses if a user owns multiple.

Meta's help center article clarifies that 'visual data' collected during AI experiences, like Live AI, may be used for training and improving AI models, involving both automated and manual (human) review. This data does not include photos and videos captured when the device's LED indicator is on.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Anthropic inks $11.6B]] 7-year cloud deal with Akamai, gets warrants
headline: Anthropic inks $11.6B 7-year cloud deal with Akamai, gets warrants
summary: The AI company's largest commitment to date includes a potential 5% stake in Anthropic for Akamai, tied to future spending.
details: Anthropic has agreed to spend $11.6 billion over seven years on Akamai's cloud infrastructure. This deal is significantly larger than a previously reported $1.8 billion agreement.

The commitment is contingent on Akamai meeting certain service availability requirements. As part of the agreement, Akamai has issued Anthropic a warrant for nonvoting preferred stock, convertible into approximately 5% of Anthropic's outstanding shares.

This marks the first time Akamai has included a warrant in a cloud deal and represents the largest contract in the company's history. The warrant's value increases as Anthropic commits more funds to Akamai's services.

The deal underscores the growing demand for general-purpose CPUs in AI, a less-hyped area compared to GPUs. Akamai expects to spend $5.5 billion to build out the necessary capacity and is increasing its capital spending to acquire components.

Akamai anticipates initial revenue from the deal in the second half of 2027, with an annual pace of about $1.7 billion by the end of 2028. This strategic move by Anthropic diversifies its compute infrastructure partnerships beyond major cloud providers like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft.
